sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Daily GitHub Trending snapshot captured 2026-10-31 01:34 UTC; date range 2026-10-31 through 2026-10-31. Ranks 1-11 use daily Trending star gains, with four recent-repository Search results appended separately.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent workflows dominate today's visible momentum: agent memory, skill-based development methods, agent-first IDEs, and design review are all represented among the highest daily gainers. A second signal is practical agent infrastructure—from private computer-use workspaces to a faster headless browser—alongside a handful of very new projects with strong early interest.

sections.title: pbakaus/impeccable
sections.description: A design vocabulary and review toolkit that helps coding agents build and critique more distinctive interfaces.
sections.why_notable: The day's largest listed gain; its README describes reusable design playbooks, deterministic UI checks, and critique/audit workflows.

sections.title: HKUDS/DeepTutor
sections.description: An open-source personalized tutoring system that uses AI to support ongoing learning.
sections.why_notable: Nearly matches the top daily gain, putting AI tutoring alongside agent tooling as a major demand signal.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: A composable skill framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Strong daily acceleration for a process-oriented toolkit whose documented workflow moves from specification to planning, testing, and subagent implementation.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent agent context that captures, compresses, and retrieves information across sessions.
sections.why_notable: Reinforces durable memory as a core agent layer; its README describes searchable session context and memory compression.

sections.title: Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu
sections.description: An open-source Chinese astrology charting engine with algorithms and a knowledge base.
sections.why_notable: A notable non-agent, culturally specific application among the day's leading gainers, with a substantial data and interpretation component described in its README.

sections.title: pingdotgg/t3code
sections.description: An open, remote-ready control surface for coding agents running on a developer's machines.
sections.why_notable: Its mobile, web, and desktop clients point to growing interest in supervising local coding agents from multiple devices.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: An open-source workspace for running and coordinating personal AI bots.
sections.why_notable: The README emphasizes local-first, bring-your-own-agent bots with separate personalities, models, and connected apps.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: A collection of small, composable engineering skills for AI agents.
sections.why_notable: Its gain supports the shift toward reusable, adaptable skills rather than one all-encompassing development process.

sections.title: JetBrains/thinkrail
sections.description: An agentic IDE built around the pi coding agent, isolated workspaces, and project knowledge.
sections.why_notable: A major IDE vendor's experimental project is applying living specs and reusable skills to personalize an agentic development environment.

sections.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot
sections.description: A self-hosted template for AI coworkers with individual browsers, files, and controlled tools.
sections.why_notable: It makes agent action review and a dedicated computer environment explicit design choices; the project describes itself as an early template, not a hosted product.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels it beta and describes it as a template to clone and customize, not a hosted service.

sections.title: lightpanda-io/browser
sections.description: A headless browser written in Zig and designed for AI agents and automation.
sections.why_notable: A distinct infrastructure bet in a list otherwise dominated by agent applications and workflows: a browser built from scratch rather than a Chromium fork.

sections.title: valentderah/totk-pc-recomp
sections.description: A static recompilation project targeting a native Windows version of Tears of the Kingdom.
sections.why_notable: Created on 2026-10-29 and surfaced in recent-repository search with substantial early stars; GitHub Trending did not supply its daily gain in this capture.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says game files are not included, users need their own legally obtained copy, and the project is in early development with visual bugs and crashes expected.

sections.title: wangzan101/Mika
sections.description: An on-device Android agent that operates apps and the web to carry out user requests.
sections.why_notable: A newly created mobile-agent project with early traction, using a background screen so users can continue using their phone.
sections.unique_caveat: The README specifies Android 13 or later and an arm64 device/sandbox.

sections.title: heydamir/unslop
sections.description: A Claude skill that reviews and redesigns generic-looking AI-generated interfaces.
sections.why_notable: Created on 2026-10-29; it joins the design-tooling signal with a concrete audit-before-edit workflow.
sections.unique_caveat: The README documents it as a Claude skill; broader harness support was not established from the README reviewed.

sections.title: paipiange/nvzhuang
sections.description: A bilingual AI fashion-reference gallery with an optional virtual try-on backend.
sections.why_notable: A recently created, fast-starred applied-AI project outside the coding-agent cluster, combining image discovery with optional model-powered try-on.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the try-on feature needs a self-hosted backend and the user's own model API key; the gallery itself is static.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent skills and repeatable workflows (Impeccable, Superpowers, mattpocock/skills); memory and persistent agent workspaces (claude-mem, ThinkRail, OpenMausBot, OpenBot); agentic IDEs and remote control (T3 Code, ThinkRail); design quality for AI-generated software (Impeccable, unslop); agent execution infrastructure (Lightpanda, OpenBot); applied AI learning (DeepTutor); mobile agents (Mika); specialized applied projects (TotK recompilation, ziwei-doushu, nvzhuang). Language tally across the 15 entries: TypeScript 6, Shell 2, and Rust, Python, Zig, C, Kotlin, JavaScript, and Go one each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is the operational layer around coding agents: persistent memory, reusable engineering skills, agent-aware IDEs, design critique, and controllable execution environments. The recent-repository search broadens that picture with an on-device Android agent and a pair of new, focused design/media tools, but their current star totals are not comparable to the Trending page's daily-gain figures. Together, the list suggests developers are investing not only in agent capability, but in making agent work persistent, reviewable, and usable in real workflows.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending (captured 2026-10-31 01:34 UTC). Corroboration: GitHub REST repository and default-branch-ref endpoints for selected repositories; GitHub Search query created:2026-10-29..2026-10-31 pushed:>=2026-10-29 stars:>1000 for fresh candidates; selected first-party READMEs checked. Ranks 1-11 follow daily stars today; four recent Search results appended separately with unavailable daily gains. No prior-window comparison was gathered.
